source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 campus in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 110,000 square feet, and that 9 MW is the only power figure the operator discloses.

The certifications are the more specific signal. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 qualify the facility for payment, health, federal, and audited workloads. None of them name a tenant, and CyrusOne publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant roster. Any conversion of 9 MW into racks or GPUs is a modeling assumption, not a disclosed specification.

Texas has 137 mapped facilities, but only 19 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 475.41 MW. SAT1 ranks 14th in the state by published megawatts, which places it mid-sized among the small subset that discloses anything at all. The 118 silent facilities are the real context, and they are the reason a state rank says less than it appears to.

What the data does not cover is expansion. The suitability score of 56 lists announced expansion as missing, so nothing here indicates whether SAT1's 9 MW is fixed or growing. For AI specifically, the binding question is the same one the published record cannot answer: how much power the campus can actually draw, and whether that number is moving.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
